newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian shares fail to break above 1,400 points.
newsitem.headline: Austrian shares fail to break above 1,400 points.

text.p: Austria's ATX index took a shot at the 1,400 level on Monday before slipping back to end just 0.5 percent higher, and traders said the market was unlikely to breach key psychological resistance this week.
The blue-chip index finished at 1,393.90, 7.05 points up on the day but below an intra-day high of 1,400.51. Last Wednesday the ATX set a record closing high of 1,399.4.
"Quite simply, Vienna does not want to go above 1,400 points," a trader said, adding that fresh sell orders were taking the steam out of every rally.

Index heavyweights were particularly vulnerable to selling, market participants said. They forecast the ATX would hover around current levels until the expiry of July ATX futures on Friday. July ATX future finished five points at 1,402.
"Some of the local banks seem to have a vested interest in lower prices," a trader said.
Overall 13 ATX shares finished higher, seven lower and one unchanged.
Luxury hosiery maker Wolford, which presents its 1996/1997 results next week, was the top gainer. Its shares climbed 50 schillings, or 4.07 percent, to 1,280.
Steelmaker VA Stahl and brewer BBAG were also among the gainers.
Creditanstalt ordinary and preferred shares firmed as investors speculated on a favourable exchange ratio for shares in new owner Bank Austria , dealers said.
"A spread is forming of around 35 percent in the preference shares and 30 percent in the ordinaries," said one.
Moody's decision to downgrade Bank Austria's long-term credit rating and upgrade Creditanstalt's was widely expected, dealers noted.
Utilities EVN and Verbund led the decliners. Lower Austrian firm EVN ended 36 schillings, or 2.28 percent, down at 1,544.
The broad-based Vienna bourse index closed 2.11 points up at 502.37. -- Vienna newsroom, +431 531 12257
